description.value: The study used functional magnetic resonance imaging to investigate neural systems associated with romantic rejection in people who remained intensely in love with their rejecting partner, during viewing of rejecter and neutral photographs.

spans.text: To begin to identify the neural systems associated with this natural loss state, we used functional magnetic resonance imaging to study 10 women and 5 men who had recently been rejected by a partner but reported they were still intensely “in love.” Participants alternately viewed a photograph of their rejecting beloved and a photograph of a familiar, individual, interspersed with a distraction-attention task.

value: Viewing the rejecter relative to the neutral photograph produced significant activation in reward-, motivation-, craving-, and emotion-regulation-related regions, including bilateral VTA, ventral striatum, orbitofrontal/prefrontal cortex, insula, and cingulate cortex. These findings suggest that romantic rejection engages reward/loss, addiction, and emotion-regulation systems.

value: Passionate Love Scale scores were positively associated with activity in the body of the caudate nucleus and septum/fornix area. The magnitude of the caudate correlation was the same as in happily-in-love participants, while additional cortical regions associated with cocaine craving, risk aversion, and switch-versus-stay learning were also correlated with PLS scores.
